subject: Information Theory
title: Noise Is Inevitable
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Noise Is Inevitable.

hook.text: Every cable, wireless link, and hard drive introduces random errors. Perfect transmission is physically impossible.

buildup.text: Thermal noise, cosmic rays, and electrical interference flip bits at random during transmission and storage.

discovery.text: Shannon modeled this as a noisy channel: input bits go in, some get flipped, corrupted bits come out.

twist.text: You can't eliminate noise. But Shannon proved you can communicate perfectly through it—with the right code.

climax.text: Error correction doesn't fight noise. It adds enough structure that the message survives despite the noise.

punchline.text: Noise is physics. Error correction is math fighting back.

quiz.question: According to Shannon, can you communicate perfectly through a noisy channel?
options: Yes, with the right error-correcting code
Only by eliminating all noise first
